newsitem.title: USA: Fruit of the Loom to buy back shares.
newsitem.headline: Fruit of the Loom to buy back shares.

text.p: Fruit of the Loom Inc said Tuesday that its board of directors has authorized the purchase of up to $200 million of common stock in open market and privately negotiated transactions.
This represents about seven percent of its shares outstanding, which totaled 76.4 million as of October 31.

"We believe the current market value of Fruit of the Loom common stock does not reflect the underlying strengths of the company -- its customers, products and the markets it serves, as well as its strong financial position," William Farley, chairman, said in a statement.
"Our investment decision to purchase the company's stock reinforces management's long-term commitment and confidence in Fruit of the Loom's future."
The company said it also completed the previously announced sale of its hosiery business to Renfro Corp of Mount Airy, N.C.

The deal, which was effective November 8, includes the sale of substantially all the assets of the hosiery manufacturing operations for $74 million and the liquidation of other related assets, mostly accounts receivable, for about $16 million.

Fruit of the Loom said it granted Renfro an exclusive license to use the Fruit of the Loom trade name and trademarks for the manufacture, sale and distribution of athletic, casual and dress socks for adults and children.
Fruit of the Loom also said its employees involved in hosiery operations will join Renfro.
